seat.BEST_WHY: The floor. In 3, the stone blocks in the lit area (roughly x 190–560, y 460–720) are laid in a running bond where the block widths vary along a course, the joints are not a single value — some are a dark 1px line, some open into a 2–3px gap with a lighter mortar showing — and each block face carries its own directional scratch hatching (see the blocks at ~x 420–520, y 560–620, where the hatch direction changes block to block). The wall-face strip at y 425–455 has small brick with dark vertical driven pins at irregular spacing (x ≈ 230, 300, 380, 450), which reads as the orcs' repairs without announcing itself. The light falls off smoothly and warm-to-cool across the room, and the block detail survives in the half-lit zone rather than being crushed to black. Nothing is pasted on top of it, which is why it ranks above the two frames that share the same base.
seat.WORST_WHY: Every surface is a flat fill. The grey tiles (left column x 0–170 and the bottom band y 640–800 in the enlarged view) are a single value with a uniform 1px joint grid and no edge shading on any tile; the same teal moss blob is stamped unchanged at least three times (top-left ~x 60–140, y 160–240; bottom-left ~x 40–120, y 620–700; right edge ~x 1080–1140, y 450–520). The dirt floor is a brown base with red-speckle noise and no structure — no wear paths, no edge against the grey tiles, it simply butts up. The water at x 745–1030 is a hexagonal pattern fill with round bright-green lily pads on it. The two barrels at y 585–650 are pixel-identical clones, as are the two crate+slat units at x 190–290. The bottom dark-brick wall row has a lighter rectangle at ~x 490–560, y 815–830 that reads as a mis-set tile. There is no lighting anywhere in the frame. It looks like a tileset test scene.

Neither timber prop has a contact shadow; both float.

The wall masses (x 120–440, y 60–140; x 120–180, y 140–400; x 570–750, y 60–140) are a soft brown mottled fill next to a pixel-crisp floor; draw them at the floor's density.
The crack lines (from (240,520) to (420,470) and the arc at (560–750, 630–750)) cross joints without deflecting; route or break them per block.
The tiles under the player (x 380–470, y 470–560) are blown out; cap the light at the source.

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.

law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.
